title: Define canonical NO_SYNC timestamp semantics on the DIO wire
description: Spec/interop review finding. DioTimeOption permits Stratum.NO_SYNC with any unsigned 32-bit Unix timestamp at python/src/lichen/timing/time_sync.py:120-167, and python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:115-118 explicitly tests both zero and 0xffffffff. StratumTracker rejects any adopted NO_SYNC timestamp at lines 182-188, while spec/09-packets-timing.md:201-223 defines stratum 0 as no sync with monotonic counters only and the option timestamp as Unix epoch seconds. The wire meaning of a nonzero timestamp at NO_SYNC is therefore contradictory and non-canonical across encoders, decoders, and state handling.
acceptance_criteria: Specify one canonical interoperable rule for the timestamp field when stratum is NO_SYNC. Prefer requiring zero and rejecting nonzero on construction and decode; if the WG instead permits arbitrary bits, state that receivers MUST ignore them and require encoders to emit one canonical value. Update normative spec, Python, Rust, Zephyr/C, and canonical vectors consistently. Add positive canonical encoding plus negative/non-canonical decode tests, verify NO_SYNC cannot establish wall clock or enter tracker state, and exercise mixed-implementation vector parity. Run focused tests and three code-review passes per modified source module.
